paragraphs: Attaching i-cord to the edge of a knitted piece adds a nice finishing touch. There are unlimited variations to this technique. Here are three for you to try. The first is plain i-cord along the edge. The second adds a few extra rows in between and is a variation of the worm trim that you may know.

I've heard the third call a helicopter trim. Watch and see why this is a very appropriate name. Begin by casting on three stitches. Designer your machine to slip in one direction. If you aren't familiar with this, look for the Knit It Now video on knitting i-cord.

Pick up one loop of the knitted garment and hang it on the end needle. This could be an edge stitch or a stitch on the caston or bound off edge. Knit across and back, slipping in one direction. Repeat this across the edge of the piece you're finishing.

Try this technique first on your swatch to check the gauge. But I generally use the garment tension to knit an i-cord edge. When you get to a corner, just knit a couple of extra rows without picking up the garment stitch. Keep picking up and knitting.

Picking up and knitting and soon you'll see that you have a beautiful edge that looks great on both sides. The second i-cord edge is done the same way, except you knit a few rows between the pickup. In this example, we're knitting three rows with six passes of the carriage before picking up the next stitch.

Pick up the next stitch or skip a few. Try it both ways again. Try this on a swatch. It tends to flare and may not be appropriate for your project. The helicopter trim is done similarly to the previous edge, but the trim is twisted before you pick up the next stitch.

As before, we're knitting three rows with six passages of the carriage. Then turn the work for a few turns and make sure the private side of the work is facing you again. Then pick up the next stitch of your knitted piece.

Repeat this across the row. Again, you can pick up the next stitch or skip a few rows as you can see. See, the number of turns determines the shape of the twisted i-cord that forms. Mastering i-cord will go a long way in creating your own designs.
Play and have fun with them.
